T1: Seed with activity, a split pull hitting 3+ victims, a kit approval amount, a bait contract with 3+ paying victims, or another kit-confirmed drain.
T2: A split pull with 1-2 victims, payments to a known operator, a kit fingerprint with activity, or a twin of a T1 on another chain.
T3: Code or behaviour that fits a drainer without a confirmed drain: red-flag selectors, multi-victim pulls alone, 7702 sweepers, single EOA pulls.

deploy_drain: Deploy and drain in one tx
The contract was created in the same transaction that moved a victim's tokens.
ghost_forward: Tokens left an address with no code and no transactions of its own: code that existed only inside the transaction.
ghost_forward_multi: Such a one-transaction contract moved tokens of two or more addresses.
bait_forward: A victim paid a function and most of the value left to third addresses in the same transaction.
bait_forward_multi: Two or more victims paid it and the value was forwarded on.
kept_share: The contract kept a share of the forwarded value, like a fee.
token_spender_pull: An ERC-20-like contract with DELEGATECALL pulled tokens from the wallets that approved it.
token_spender_multi: It pulled tokens from two or more approving wallets.
owner_takeover: Became the owner of a contract and then moved tokens out of it.
owner_takeover_multi: Took over and emptied two or more contracts.
safe_spender: A Safe proxy that three or more wallets approved as a spender.
safe_spender_pull: That Safe proxy also pulled tokens from wallets that approved it.
safe_approval: A wallet approved this Safe proxy as a spender.
safe_pull: This Safe proxy pulled a wallet's approved tokens.
seaport_zero: Filled a Seaport order where the victim gave NFTs and received nothing.
seaport_zero_multi: Filled such orders for two or more victims.
nft_operator_pull: A wallet set this address as operator for all its NFTs, and it then moved them.
batch7702_approve: A victim's EIP-7702 account sent itself a batch that approved this wallet and moved tokens out.
eip7702_batch: Many EIP-7702 authorizations to this delegate in one transaction.
eip7702_chain0: Authorizations signed with chainId 0, valid on every EVM chain.
share_grid: The split shares sit on the documented drainer-as-a-service grid (70, 80, 85 or 90 %).
vanity_drainer: A look-alike vanity address that wallets approved or that drained them.
vanity_approval: A wallet approved this vanity-address spender.
operator_wallet: Payout wallet of two or more flagged drainers.
operator_wallet_multi: Payout wallet of several drainers that have their own strong evidence.
serial_deployer: Deployed two or more flagged contracts.
serial_deployer_multi: Deployed several flagged contracts that have their own strong evidence.
tron_split_capped: TRON split without kit code, capped at T3
A split pull on TRON with fewer than three victims and no drainer-kit or puller code: payment splitters and forwarders look the same.
zero_transfer_spoof: Zero-value transferFrom legs out of other people's wallets (address poisoning).
contract_lookups_capped: The per-run limit of code lookups was reached; some code was not checked.
seed: Listed by ScamSniffer or the operator seed file, and seen active here.
seed_activity: A victim approved or sent tokens to a known drainer address.
split_pull: One transaction pulled a victim's token and split it between two or more wallets, the drainer-as-a-service fee pattern.
spoof_split: Looks like a split pull but behaves like address poisoning, not a real drain.
multi_victim_pull: Pulled tokens from three or more approving wallets within 24 hours.
eoa_spender_pull: A plain wallet pulled another wallet's tokens straight to a third wallet.
eoa_spender_multi: The same pulling wallet hit three or more victims within 24 hours.
pays_known_operator: Sent tokens to a known drainer payout wallet in two or more transactions.
pays_inferred_operator: Sent tokens to payout wallets we only inferred; capped at suspect.
redflag_selectors: The code exposes kit function names such as Claim() or SecurityUpdate().
family_match: The code skeleton or function set matches a known drainer contract.
bytecode: Opcode skeleton, function selectors and family comparison of the contract code.
eip7702_sweeper: An EIP-7702 delegate that forwards whatever value arrives; delegating wallets are potential victims.
redflag_payable: A victim sent coins to a red-flag function such as Claim().
approval_fingerprint: A victim approved exactly the amount hard-coded in a drainer kit.
bait_payable: A victim paid a bait function; its argument is the kit customer's payout wallet.
bait_withdraw: A kit customer withdrew from the bait contract.
kit_signature: The contract's function set matches a known drainer kit.
owner_gated_puller: A small contract that only its owner can use to pull approved tokens to any address.
split_xtx: Same caller, victim and token split over two or more transactions within 60 seconds.
foreign_recipient_swap: A victim-signed swap with zero minimum output that paid this wallet instead of the signer.
foreign_swap_multi: Such swaps for three or more victims within 24 hours.
foreign_swap_kit: The swap deadline is block time plus about 99 990 seconds, the MS Drainer kit value.
owner_collect: An owner-collector contract pulled a victim's tokens to its caller.
ms_deadline: A permit whose deadline is in milliseconds, a drainer-kit tell.
ms_deadline_pull: Tokens left the owner right after the millisecond-deadline permit.
batch_approval_drain: A batch of kit-amount or unlimited approvals drained to this wallet in one transaction.
kit_router_swap: A kit-amount approval to a real router, followed by the same drain.
kit_deposit: A fresh wallet sent nearly its whole balance to the kit Deposit function.
gen_back_transfer: The deployer sent its leftover coins to a kit wallet after deploying a generated bait.
kit_exact: The code is byte-for-byte one of the known MS Contract Generator baits.
kit_public: The code is byte-for-byte one of the drainer kit's shared public contracts.
kit_confirmed: A victim paid a bait function of one of the kit's shared public contracts.
ms_cashback: An MS_NEW bait call asked to send 1 wei back to the victim, a kit tell.
ms_cashback_shape: A payable call carried the MS_NEW cashback flag, but the code is not the kit's.
dust_approve: An approval sent with a few wei attached, a kit quirk.
dust_approve_kit: Such an approval also used the kit's hard-coded amount.
emergency_gas: Sent a small amount of gas to a wallet that approved it, or a flagged spender, within 30 minutes.
emergency_gas_self: Funded a wallet that then approved the funder; also the shape of exchange deposit sweeping, so a weak lead.
emergency_gas_kit: Such an approval used the kit's hard-coded amount.
kit_vanity: The address starts with 0x000 and ends with 0000, like the kit's contracts; raises the score only.
oneshot_spender: A fresh wallet pulled a third party's tokens for this hub.
oneshot_hub: Its one-shot workers sent their leftover gas back here.
oneshot_multi: Three or more one-shot workers returned their leftover here.
prefund_hub: Funded fresh wallets shortly before they pulled victims' tokens.
prefund_multi: Prefunded three or more such workers.
eip7702_operator: The hub or collector is an EIP-7702-delegated wallet; raises the score only.
cross_chain: The same address with the same code is flagged on another chain.
cross_chain_t1: The same address and code is confirmed (T1) on another chain.
cluster_inherited: Tier raised because it shares payout wallets with a better-evidenced cluster member.
wa_scam: The wallet-attribution dataset labels this address scam or hack.
unpriced_capped: Unpriced single split, capped at T3
One victim, an unpriced token and no other evidence: token fee/tax routers split the same way.
kit_pull: Tokens of a third party were pulled through a contract whose dispatcher matches a drainer kit or an owner-gated parametric puller.
approval_kit_shape: An approval of exactly 10^46 units, the amount hard-coded by a TRON approval kit (with its 35 TRX fee limit it is a T1 fingerprint).
approve_all_call: The victim called the unidentified token method daea85c5(address) for this spender, an approval trick used by a TRON kit.
aml_approve_transfer: Approve of the exact balance with a 300 TRX fee limit followed by a transfer of 0 or of the whole balance to the same spender.
increase_max: Unlimited increaseApproval to a spender less than 30 days old or to a puller contract.
prefund_approve: Sent a small whole amount of TRX to a wallet that then approved this wallet or a contract it created.
prefund_approve_multi: Three or more wallets got the same TRX amount and then approved a spender of this wallet.
claimer_split: A payable bait call that took min(balance - 50 TRX, 80% of balance), the native-coin rule of a TRON kit.
perm_hijack: An account at least 30 days old changed its permissions so its own key is no longer enough and this key alone (or this key together with the key of the account) can sign; several foreign keys that must co-sign (organisation multisig) are not counted.
perm_hijack_multi: The same controller key took over three or more accounts (T2; T1 needs a drain signed by the key).
perm_hijack_drain: Funds left a taken-over account in a transaction signed by this controller key.
fixed_fee: Received the same whole TRX amount right after pulls of tokens of other people, two or more times.
fixed_fee_multi: Fixed fee, three or more victims
The same fixed TRX fee followed pulls from three or more victims.
poison_zero: Moved 0 USDT out of wallets of other people to look-alike addresses (address poisoning). Never above T3.
verified_capped: Etherscan shows verified source code and the only evidence is a split or multi-victim pull; drainers are almost never verified.

ms_drainer: Bait function taking the customer wallet, plus the kit's companion functions.
verify_account: Puller with Verify20, Verify10 and withdrawAllTrxTo functions.
ms_new: Public MS_NEW contract: five-argument bait functions plus salary and receiver controls.
ms_generated: Bait produced by the MS Contract Generator.
trusty_v1: The kit's 2023 public pass-through contract: bait functions taking the customer wallet, plus fee controls.
owner_collector: Five or more owner-collect functions such as collectToOwner and rescueToken.
buytron_swap_trx: TRON fake TRX-purchase kit: pullFunds, admin and token functions only.
buytron_swap_proxy: TRON fake TRX-purchase kit, older contract: transferFrom, usdt and owner functions only.
tron_1e46: Approval of exactly 10^46 token units, the hard-coded amount of a TRON approval kit.

affiliate: The larger share of a split pull, usually the customer who ran the phishing site. Inferred from share size.
operator: The smaller share of a split pull, usually the kit operator's fee. Inferred from share size.
customer: Kit customer payout wallet: the bait function argument or the withdraw caller. No share observed.
collector: Received tokens pulled by a wallet-to-wallet pull or an owner-collector. No share observed.
worker: One-shot wallet or MS_NEW keeper doing pulls for this hub.
kit_fee: Fee receiver configured in a generated bait.
kit_wallet: Received the generator deployer's leftover coins.
funder: Sent the victim a small amount of TRX for fees shortly before the victim approved this spender.

VIA.toplevel: Creation transaction seen by the scanner
VIA.unknown: Unknown: not visible and never guessed
